normative_extracts.spec_section: HTML Living Standard §7.2.4 Cross-origin opener policies
normative_extracts.quote: A document becomes cross-origin isolated when served with Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin and a Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy of require-corp or credentialless, isolating its browsing context group.

engine_internals.mechanism_summary: COOP severs window.opener links to cross-origin popups while COEP blocks unauthenticated cross-origin bytes, allowing the OS process to safely expose SharedArrayBuffer and microsecond timers.

production_failures.symptom: Third-party CDN images and analytics scripts fail with ERR_BLOCKED_BY_RESPONSE.NotSameOriginAfterDefaultedToSameOriginByCoep
production_failures.root_cause: Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp blocks every cross-origin subresource lacking Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin or CORS headers.
production_failures.mitigation: Add crossorigin='anonymous' with CORS headers on CDN assets, or use COEP: credentialless (where supported) so uncredentialed fetches succeed without CORP.

production_failures.symptom: OAuth popup window.opener becomes null and breaks postMessage login callback
production_failures.root_cause: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin severs window.opener across origins, blocking popup-to-opener postMessage.
production_failures.mitigation: Use same-origin-allow-popups when isolation is not needed, or switch OAuth callbacks to same-origin redirect + BroadcastChannel.
